exposure: Transfer of more than two embryos without embryo cryopreservation (TET)
outcome: Multiple delivery rate (twin deliveries, triplets and more deliveries)
cohort: The study included 11,024 women undergoing elective dual embryo transfer (eDET) and 10,634 women undergoing transfer of more than two embryos (TET) from 155 clinics registered with the Latin American Registry of Assisted Reproductive Techniques.
finding: Elective dual embryo transfer (eDET) resulted in a statistically significantly better delivery rate and a lower ratio of triplet-and-higher deliveries compared to the transfer of more than two embryos (TET), regardless of the woman's age.
